ops.quote: Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) can be applied to graph similarity matching
The DGCL uses a mixed Gaussian function to realize the mapping between the convolution kernel and the nodes in the neighborhood of the graph
The output of the DGCL is the input of the CNN
We further implement a backward-propagation optimization process of the convolutional layer
the optimization of the convolution kernel becomes part of the neural network learning process
The DGC/N can accept arbitrary scaled and disordered neighborhood graph structures as the receptive fields of CNNs
which reduces information loss during graph transformation
the results show that the proposed method outperforms the state-of-the-art methods in graph classification and retrieval
